newsitem.title: USA: Mexico US certification faces uphill fight - Daschle.
newsitem.headline: Mexico US certification faces uphill fight - Daschle.

text.p: Senate Minority Leader Tom Daschle said Monday President Clinton's proposed re-certification of Mexico as an ally in the drug war faced an uphill battle to clear the Senate.

The South Dakota Democrat said he favors continued certification but noted that opponents have gathered 40 co-sponsors on a resolution of disapproval. Democratic Sen. Diane Feinstein of California will introduce the disapproval resolution.
"It will be an uphill battle to keep what the president has done (recommended recertification). I think Sen. Feinstein has hit a nerve here," he said at his regular press briefing.
Recertification of Mexico as a U.S. ally in the drug war avoids a cut-off in some U.S. aid and economic sanctions.
Clinton recommended recertification Feb. 28 despite serious problems and congressional opposition.

Daschle said he favors the recertification because Mexico has made progress. "You can cite all the accomplishments and make a pretty good case, as the president has with me and others that they deserve recertification."
"We have set pretty high expectations. Have they met all those expectations? Of course not. Are they making a good faith effort? Well, that is a judgmental call," Daschle said.
